source.title: A Modern Take on the Bias-Variance Tradeoff in Neural Networks
source.authors: Brady Neal; Sarthak Mittal; A. Baratin; Vinayak Tantia; M. Scicluna; Simon Lacoste-Julien; Ioannis Mitliagkas

record.file_problem: Full text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Measures bias, variance, and test error across widths of fully connected networks, using a different measurement focus from the mapped width claim.
record.gate_note: Tests width-related error trends and variance components. It does not test random-label memorization, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Values available only in plots are not transcribed as numbers.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own training and test classification errors across network widths, including small MNIST trained beyond training-error convergence without explicit regularization. These results bear on V2. Prediction variance alone does not measure V2's test-error claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors find that bias and variance can decrease together as width increases, with optimization variance decreasing and sampling variance increasing slowly before leveling off. Their central conclusion concerns the absence of a necessary bias-variance tradeoff with width, rather than an unconditional guarantee of decreasing classification error.
record.recipe_differences: Studies width and error trends with modern fully connected networks, SGD with momentum, and explicit measurements of bias and variance; it does not reproduce the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU test-error experiment as stated.
record.method_sensitivity: In the small-data setting, step size is tuned by network size; with a fixed step size of 0.01, bias does not monotonically decrease. The authors also report that the width-related variance trend persists with batch gradient descent and LBFGS.

fits_no_version.finding: Prediction variance decreases with width across the reported image tasks and optimizers; bias also decreases in the main experiments. Noisy sinusoid regression shows similar trends.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing neural-network width can reduce both squared-loss prediction bias and prediction variance, including with very small training sets.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimization variance decreases with width, while sampling variance increases slowly and plateaus in sufficiently overparameterized networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prediction variance has distinct optimization and sampling components with different width dependence.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing depth can raise test error despite zero training error and matched training loss; dynamical isometry substantially reduces the degradation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization trends with depth depend on initialization and architecture and can differ from width trends.

record.problems: Width trends are mostly reported qualitatively or in plots; exact error values are not stated in the text. The small-data experiment tunes step size per network size. Bias estimation uses labels as an estimate of the conditional expected label, equivalent to assuming noiseless labels.
record.rows_left_out: No separate width rows for train/test error on CIFAR10, SVHN, or sinusoid regression were extracted because the relevant values are figure-only and the text does not state their trends individually. The appendix figures B.1, B.2, B.7, and Figure 19 contain plotted curves.

untested.parts: Matched random-label memorization and natural-label generalization experiments.
The exact interpolation threshold, a test-error peak near it, and the specified downsampled CIFAR-10 setup are not established by the supplied text. ReLU activation is not specified.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under matched tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Adding or removing dropout and its effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Small-MNIST training and test classification errors with fixed learning rate 0.01, including the explicitly discussed U-shaped curve and whether its rising segment follows interpolation.

Full-data MNIST test classification error across widths. R1 records only prediction variance, and rows_left_out does not declare omission of this test-error result. Curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

Small-MNIST classification-error width sweeps for batch gradient descent and LBFGS; R6 and R7 capture only prediction variance. Extract test-error trends and available training-error evidence from the plots.

record.verdict_notes: Unavailable numerical plot values do not themselves justify limits_scope. R3 has an explicit qualitative test-error result. The other original V2 links incorrectly treated prediction variance as classification-error evidence. CIFAR-10, SVHN, and sinusoid test-error plot omissions were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test accuracy.
The specified downsampled CIFAR-10 setup and the precise interpolation threshold are not stated as tested conditions.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparison and local connectivity.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
